Package com.example.inelasticsearch.cluster

Class ClusterTopology

java.lang.Object
com.example.inelasticsearch.cluster.ClusterTopology
public class ClusterTopology extends Object
The cluster's static routing table: how many shards an index is split into, how many replica copies each shard gets, and which NodeAddresses make up the cluster. Every process (coordinator or data node) loads the same cluster.conf into one of these, so routing decisions are computed identically everywhere with no runtime coordination or discovery.

Three routing questions this class answers, each with a different scheme:

  • Which shard does a document belong to? (shardFor(java.lang.String)) — hash the document id mod totalShards. Statistically even for a diverse set of ids, but not a measured or enforced balance.
  • Which node is a shard's primary? (nodeFor(int)) — shardId % nodes.size(). Plain round-robin, exactly even when totalShards is a multiple of the node count.
  • Which nodes hold a shard's replicas? (replicaNodesFor(int)) — the next replicaCount nodes after the primary in ring order, so a shard's primary and replicas are always on different nodes.

This is a fixed assignment for the process lifetime: there is no rebalancing if the node list changes, and no cluster membership/health protocol. Restarting every process against an edited cluster.conf is how the topology changes.

  • Constructor Details

    • ClusterTopology

      public ClusterTopology(int totalShards, List<NodeAddress> nodes)
      Convenience constructor for a topology with no replicas (replicaCount = 0).

    • ClusterTopology

      public ClusterTopology(int totalShards, int replicaCount, List<NodeAddress> nodes)
      Parameters:
      totalShards - how many shards an index is split into; fixed for the life of the cluster
      replicaCount - how many replica copies of each shard to place on other nodes; clamped down to nodes.size() - 1 at lookup time if it's larger than the cluster can hold
      nodes - every node in the cluster, in the fixed order used for round-robin shard/replica placement — this order must be identical across every process sharing this config

    • parse

      static ClusterTopology parse(List<String> lines)
      Parses the key=value lines of a cluster.conf. Recognized keys: totalShards (required), replicas (optional, defaults to 0), and any other key is treated as a node id mapping to a host:port value. Blank lines and # comments (full-line or trailing) are ignored. Package-private so ClusterTopologyTest can drive it directly with in-memory config text instead of writing temp files.

    • shardFor

      public int shardFor(String docId)
      Which shard a document belongs to, by hashing its id. Independent of which node currently owns that shard — combine with nodeFor(int) to find where a document actually lives.

    • nodeFor

      public NodeAddress nodeFor(int shardId)
      The node that owns a shard's primary copy — the only node writes for that shard should go to. Plain round-robin (`shardId % nodes.size()`), so it never changes without a topology reload.

    • nodeById

      public NodeAddress nodeById(String nodeId)
      Looks up a node by its config id (e.g. "node-a"); throws if it isn't in the cluster.

    • shardsOwnedBy

      public Set<Integer> shardsOwnedBy(String nodeId)
      Every shard for which the given node is the primary (see nodeFor(int)).

    • replicaNodesFor

      public List<NodeAddress> replicaNodesFor(int shardId)
      The nodes holding replica copies of a shard, in ring order after the primary (e.g. with replicaCount = 2, the primary's next two neighbors in nodes()). Never includes the shard's own primary node. If replicaCount is larger than the cluster can support (nodes.size() - 1 distinct other nodes), it's silently clamped down rather than erroring.
